tool_calls.arguments:
{"plan": "# Project Cognition Report: commander.js (v14.0.3 snapshot @ bf35c5f)

## 1. Project Identity

- **What it is**: `commander` — "the complete solution for node.js command-line programs." A declarative CLI-parsing library: the developer describes options/commands/arguments in a fluent API; commander parses `argv`, enforces strictness, generates help/usage text, and runs action handlers or child-process subcommands.
- **Repo / lineage**: github.com/tj/commander.js (original author TJ Holowaychuk; de-facto lead maintainer John Gee/"shadowspawn" — 489 non-merge commits vs. 100+42 for Holowaychuk). 1,493 commits, 223 tracked files, MIT license.
- **Snapshot state**: clean working tree, detached HEAD at `bf35c5f` = the `14.0.3` release (`8247364`) plus 2 dependency bumps. No git tags present in this snapshot; version taken from `package.json`/`CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Scale**: runtime source ≈ 3,770 LOC across 6 files (`lib/command.js` 2,777, `lib/help.js` 747, `lib/option.js` 380, `lib/argument.js` 150, `lib/suggestSimilar.js` 101, `lib/error.js` 39) + entry points (`index.js`, `esm.mjs`). Hand-written typings 1,664 LOC. Tests: 110 Jest files ≈ 11,000 LOC (≈3× source), 45 examples, 6 docs.
- **Package surface**: `name: commander`, `version: 14.0.3`, `engines: node >= 20`, **zero runtime dependencies** (devDependencies only), dual CJS/ESM via `exports` map with `types` conditions, bundled `typings/index.d.ts` + `typings/esm.d.mts`.
- **Cadence & support**: semver; majors ~every 6 months aligned to Node LTS EOL (14.0.0 May 2025 dropped to Node ≥20; 13.x maintenance until 2026-05-18; older lines EOL — `docs/release-policy.md`, new in 14.0.3). Security via Tidelift (`SECURITY.md`), CodeQL in CI, sponsors on `package-support.json`.
- **Toolchain**: Jest (+ts-jest), `tsd` + `tsc` for typings, `tsc --checkJs` for JSDoc, ESLint 9 flat config, Prettier. CI: Node 20/22/24 × ubuntu/windows/macos (`npm test` + `npm run check`).

## 2. Architecture Map

**Package layout / module graph**
- `index.js` — CJS entry: exports `program` (a singleton `new Command()`), factories `createCommand/createOption/createArgument`, classes `Command/Option/Argument/Help`, errors `CommanderError/InvalidArgumentError` (+deprecated alias `InvalidOptionArgumentError`).
- `esm.mjs` — thin ESM wrapper re-exporting named exports (CJS core stays the single implementation).
- `typings/` — hand-maintained `index.d.ts` (1,113 LOC) mirrored by `esm.d.mts` re-export; validated by `typings/index.test-d.ts` via `tsd` and by `tests/ts-imports.test.ts` via `tsc`.
- `lib/` — the entire runtime. Cross-file edges: `command.js` → `option.js` (`Option`, `DualOptions`), `argument.js`, `error.js`, `help.js` (`Help`, `stripColor`), `suggestSimilar.js`, and Node built-ins (`events`, `child_process`, `path`, `fs`, `process`).

**Object model**
- `Command extends EventEmitter` — a command is a tree node: `parent` pointer, `commands[]`, `options[]`, `registeredArguments[]`. Subcommands created via `.command()`/`.addCommand()` inherit parent settings through `copyInheritedSettings()` (output config, help option/command, exit callback, strictness flags) — not prototypes.
- `Option` — parses the flags string (`splitOptionFlags`: one short `-x`, one or two longs `--foo, --bar`; noisy construction-time errors), carries `required/optional/variadic/negate/mandatory`, `defaultValue`, `presetArg`, `envVar`, `parseArg`, `argChoices`, `conflictsWith`, `implied`, `helpGroupHeading`.
- `Argument` — same value-model as `Option` minus env/conflicts/implies; `required/optional/variadic`, `parseArg`, `argChoices`, `defaultValue`.
- `Help` — stateless-in-style formatting engine (constructor holds only 5 config fields; all methods overridable), plus `formatHelp`, grouping, styling, wrapping.
- `CommanderError(exitCode, code, message)` + `InvalidArgumentError` (code `commander.invalidArgument`).
- `suggestSimilar` — Damerau–Levenshtein (max distance 3, min similarity 0.4) for "Did you mean…" hints.

**Parse pipeline** (the heart of the system)
```
parse()/parseAsync()
 → _prepareForParse()          save/restore state (multi-parse support since 13.0)
 → _prepareUserArgs()          argv conventions: node | electron | user | eval; derives _name from script path
 → _parseCommand(operands, unknown)
     → parseOptions()          single-pass tokenizer over args
     → _parseOptionsEnv()      env vars (only if source is default/config/env/undefined)
     → _parseOptionsImplied()  implies (dual-option aware)
     → dispatch: subcommand | help command | default command | action handler | legacy events | help-on-error
```
- `parseOptions()` (in-place, refactored in 14.0.1): recognizes exact flags, `-abc` short-flag groups, `--foo=bar`, `--` literal terminator, negative numbers (unless a numeric short option exists in the hierarchy), variadic option collection (`activeVariadicOption`), and positional/pass-through modes. Output: `{operands, unknown}` where unknown args are deferred for subcommand reprocessing.
- **Value assignment is event-driven**: `addOption()` registers `option:<name>` / `optionEnv:<name>` listeners; the tokenizer emits values; `handleOptionValue` applies `presetArg` → `parseArg`/variadic collect → fill-in defaults (negate→false, boolean/optional→true) → `setOptionValueWithSource(name, val, source)`. Sources (`default/config/env/cli/implied`) are tracked per key and drive precedence (cli > env > config > default), mandatory-option and conflict checks.
- **Dispatch & execution**: `_dispatchSubcommand` chains `preSubcommand` hooks, then either spawns an executable (`_executeSubCommand`: local-file search incl. legacy name, `.js/.ts/.mjs/…` extension probing, node-launch for source files, `stdio: 'inherit'`, signal forwarding SIGUSR1/2/TERM/INT/HUP, inspector-port increment, exit-code propagation via `process.exit` or `exitOverride`) or recursively `_parseCommand`. Hooks (`preAction`/`postAction`, ancestor-walked, postAction reversed) and action handlers are promise-chained via `_chainOrCall`.
- **Error/exit path**: `error(message, {code, exitCode})` → `configureOutput().outputError` → optional help-after-error → `_exit()` → `exitOverride` callback or `process.exit`. Stable error codes: `commander.invalidArgument`, `.missingArgument`, `.optionMissingArgument`, `.missingMandatoryOptionValue`, `.conflictingOption`, `.unknownOption`, `.unknownCommand`, `.excessArguments`, `.version`, `.help`, `.helpDisplayed`, `.executeSubCommandAsync`, `.error`.
- **Help subsystem**: `outputHelp` → `helpInformation` → `createHelp()` (subclass hook) + `configureHelp()` overrides → `prepareContext` (width/colors) → `formatHelp` (Usage / Description / Arguments / grouped Options / grouped Commands, `padWidth` alignment, `boxWrap` with `minWidthToWrap`, `style*` color hooks, `displayWidth`/`stripColor`). Output context resolves stdout/stderr, TTY width, and color support (`NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`/`CLICOLOR_FORCE` + TTY detection). Custom text via `addHelpText` (`before/after/beforeAll/afterAll` events).

## 3. Critical Components

| Component | Location | Why critical |
|---|---|---|
| `Command` monolith | `lib/command.js` (2,777 LOC) | Entire behavior lives here: registration, parsing, dispatch, errors, help, subcommand spawn. Largest blast radius in the repo. |
| `parseOptions()` | command.js:1748 | Tokenizer correctness = library correctness: `-abc` groups, `--x=v`, `--`, negative numbers, variadic capture, positional/pass-through. Subtle state machine; refactored in-place in 14.0.1 (risk of regression). |
| Value pipeline (`addOption` → `handleOptionValue` → `setOptionValueWithSource`) | command.js:670-733, 953 | Env/implied/dual-option behavior, `parseArg` error wrapping (`_callParseArg`), and source-based precedence all hinge on emit order and source bookkeeping. |
| `_parseCommand` dispatch | command.js:1550 | Decides action vs. subcommand vs. help vs. unknown-command; ordering of strictness checks (help before mandatory, mandatory before unknown-option) encodes UX decisions. |
| `_executeSubCommand` | command.js:1202 | Child-process lifecycle: file search, Windows behavior, signals, exit-code propagation, `exitOverride` async path. |
| Error/exit path (`error`, `_exit`, `exitOverride`) | command.js:533, 1940 | Tested heavily (`command.exitOverride.test.js`, 460 LOC); any change breaks programmatic embedding use cases. |
| `Help` class | `lib/help.js` | Public customization surface (`configureHelp`, `createHelp`, style methods, groups since 14.0). Formatting bugs are immediately user-visible. |
| Typings | `typings/index.d.ts` + `index.test-d.ts` | Hand-maintained second source of truth; TS consumers rely on it; `tsd`/`tsc` gates it. |
| `Option` flag parsing | `option.js:328` | Construction-time validation (13.0 breaking change) prevents silent misuse; dual-long-flag support (13.1). |

## 4. Design Decisions

1. **Zero runtime dependencies** — only devDependencies; keeps install tiny, avoids supply-chain surface; implemented with Node built-ins only.
2. **Declarative, fluent, chainable API with getter/setter overloads** (`.name()`, `.description()`, `.usage()` return value or `this`) — one method serves both; document-heavy API surface.
3. **EventEmitter as the parser's internal bus** — option values delivered via `emit('option:name', value)`; enables legacy `command:name`/`command:*`/`--help` events cheaply, but makes control flow implicit.
4. **Strict by default** — unknown options error, excess args error (13.0 breaking), mandatory-option support; opt-out via `allowUnknownOption`/`allowExcessArguments`. Deliberate UX philosophy ("Commander is strict…" README) with migration tips in CHANGELOG.
5. **Value provenance tracking** (`default/config/env/cli/implied` sources) — enables env-vs-cli precedence, conflict detection that ignores defaults, and dual-option disambiguation (`DualOptions` heuristics).
6. **Majors coupled to Node LTS EOL** — major every ~6 months bumping `engines` (Node ≥20 in 14.x; release-policy.md predicts 15.0.0 at Node 20 EOL, April 2026). 12-month security window for old majors (new commitment in 14.0.3).
7. **Dual package with CJS core + ESM wrapper** (`esm.mjs` re-exporting named exports) — single implementation, `exports` map with `require`/`import` + `types` conditions; deprecated `commander/esm.mjs` subpath retained.
8. **Hand-written typings validated by `tsd`**, plus `tsc --checkJs` over JSDoc-annotated JS — two type sources of truth, both CI-gated (deliberately lenient JS settings, strict TS settings).
9. **Help as an overridable class** (`createHelp`/`configureHelp`/subclassing, `style*` hooks, help groups in 14.0) rather than template strings — the main extensibility surface.
10. **Lazy, inherited system components** — help option/command created on demand (`_getHelpOption`/`_getHelpCommand`), settings propagated by `copyInheritedSettings` on attach, enabling `.helpOption(false)`/`.helpCommand(false)` and consistent subcommand behavior.
11. **Backward-compat with a documented deprecation ladder** (`docs/deprecated.md`): RegExp parseArg, `noHelp`, `addHelpCommand(string)`, `InvalidOptionArgumentError`, `_args`, `command:*` events, callback to `outputHelp` — removed only across majors.
12. **Re-parseable programs** — `saveStateBeforeParse`/`restoreStateBeforeParse` (13.0) allow multiple `.parse()` calls; `storeOptionsAsProperties` legacy mode restricts this.
13. **Noisy failures at construction/registration** — duplicate flags/commands, malformed flag strings, broken pass-through config, variadic-not-last all throw early with multi-line, actionable messages.
14. **Testing philosophy** — ~110 feature-named Jest files (`command.*`, `options.*`, `help.*`, `argument.*`) exercising behavior via `parse(['…'], {from:'user'})`; mocked-spawn and real-fixture tests for executable subcommands; ESM import smoke test; strictness and error-text assertions.

## 5. Risk Map

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Notes / Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command.js` monolith fragility | High | High | 2,777-LOC class; parse/dispatch/error paths interlock. Mitigated by 10,978 LOC of tests; ongoing incremental refactors (14.0.1 in-place `parseOptions`, `_collectValue`). |
| Maintainer bus factor | Medium | High | One dominant maintainer; dependabot dominates recent history. Sponsors exist; docs/release-policy formalize process. |
| Regression in subtle parser behaviors | Medium | High | Negative numbers, `-f80` combining, dual-option value attribution, unknown-arg state transitions are heuristic-laden; hard to reason about, well tested but not exhaustively. |
| Typings drift from JSDoc/runtime | Medium | Medium | Hand-maintained `index.d.ts`; `tsd`/`checkJs` catch drift at check time but not semantic mismatches (e.g., 14.0.3's `outputHelp` callback typing clarification). |
| Breaking-change backlash at majors | Medium | Medium | 13.0 (excess args) and 14.0 (Node ≥20) broke real consumers; mitigated by migration-tip sections, 12-month maintenance window, deprecation ladder. |
| Cross-platform divergence | Low-Medium | Medium | Windows spawn path differs (always node-launched, existence pre-check); signals/paths/`EACCES` handled, CI covers 3 OSes. |
| Help-system complexity creep | Medium | Medium | Groups + styling + wrapping + global options interact (`padWidth`, `boxWrap`, ANSI width); many `help.*.test.js` files guard it. |
| Security of subcommand spawn | Low | Medium | `stdio: 'inherit'`, no shell, signal forwarding; still, executable resolution and env-based values are input surfaces; CodeQL enabled. |
| Dependency churn noise | High | Low | 135 dependabot commits; dev-only, so supply-chain exposure is limited, but review burden is real. |

## 6. Change Impact Analysis

Mapping likely change areas to blast radius (files → tests → consumers):

| Change area | Files touched | Test surface | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| New option/argument feature | `lib/option.js`, `lib/argument.js`, `command.js` (`addOption`, `parseOptions`, `_parseOptionsEnv/Implied`), `help.js`, `typings/index.d.ts` | `options.*`, `argument.*`, `help.optionDescription` | Value pipeline and source precedence must stay consistent; typings + README required. |
| Parser behavior change | `command.js:parseOptions` + dispatch | `command.parseOptions`, `command.parse`, `args.*`, `negatives`, `command.positionalOptions` | Highest regression risk; needs CHANGELOG migration tips if defaults change. |
| Error messages/codes/exit behavior | `command.js` error helpers, `error.js` | `command.error`, `command.exitOverride`, `command.showHelpAfterError` | Consumers match on codes and stderr text; codes are quasi-public API. |
| Help formatting | `help.js`, `command.js` (`outputHelp`/`helpInformation`/`_getOutputContext`) | `help.*` (20+ files), `useColor`, `helpGroup` | Custom Help subclasses in the wild will break on method signature changes (13.0 `wrap()` → `formatItem`/`boxWrap` precedent). |
| Subcommand execution | `command.js:_executeSubCommand` + helpers | `command.executableSubcommand.*` (7 files), `incrementNodeInspectorPort` | Windows + signals + exitOverride interplay; fixture-based tests. |
| Typings | `typings/index.d.ts`, `esm.d.mts`, `index.test-d.ts`, `tests/ts-imports.test.ts` | `tsd`, `tsc` gates | Additive only in minors; breaking type changes require major (TS consumers are strict). |
| Node version policy | `package.json.engines`, CI matrix, `tsconfig*.json` | CI | Next major (15.0.0) expected ~Node 20 EOL (2026-04); drop Node 20, likely add Node 26. |
| Deprecation removals | any; tracked in `docs/deprecated.md` | `deprecated.test.js` | Only in majors; each removal is a downstream breaking change. |
| Docs/examples | `Readme.md`, `Readme_zh-CN.md`, `docs/*`, `examples/*` | — | README examples are contract-level documentation; keep in sync with behavior. |

**Data-flow guidance for implementers**: value flow is one-directional (tokenizer → events → `_optionValues` + `_optionValueSources`); state restoration is shallow (objects are re-spread), so storing mutable defaults in options is unsafe across repeated `parse()`; help output must always pass through `_getOutputContext` so color/width/stripColor invariants hold.

## 7. Decision Memo

**Context**: post-14.0.3 snapshot; 14.x is the current line (Node ≥20), 13.x in 12-month maintenance. The codebase is mature, extremely well tested, and change-averse by design.

**Recommendations**:

1. **Adopt an explicit "no behavior changes in 14.x" posture.** The 14.0.1 parser refactor and 14.0.3 policy work suggest the maintainers are consolidating; treat any parse-dispatch change as major-candidate material, with CHANGELOG migration tips, per established precedent.
2. **Plan 15.0.0 against Node 20 EOL (April 2026)** — per release-policy.md this is the expected trigger; scope it early: drop Node 20, remove the last legacy paths (`_args`, RegExp parseArg, `addHelpCommand(string)`, `InvalidOptionArgumentError`), and re-verify the deprecated.md removals list.
3. **Contain `command.js` risk without a rewrite.** Continue the incremental style (in-place refactors with behavior-preserving tests). Highest-value targets: extracting the value-pipeline (`handleOptionValue` + sources) and the dispatch decisions into testable helpers; keep `parseOptions` fenced by its dedicated test files.
4. **Make typings a single source of truth or add a drift gate.** Consider generating `index.d.ts` from the JSDoc (or a CI diff-check); at minimum, extend `index.test-d.ts` coverage to every public overload (the 14.0.3 `outputHelp` typing fix shows drift happens).
5. **Protect the zero-dependency and strict-by-default decisions** — they are core differentiators; any proposal to add a runtime dependency or loosen defaults should require explicit justification in the Decision Memo of that change.
6. **Keep the release-policy and support commitments** (12-month window, Tidelift channel) — recently formalized (14.0.3) and now part of the project's contract with enterprise consumers.
7. **Reduce dependabot review noise** — batch dev-dependency bumps or use grouping, so maintainer attention stays on behavior changes (recent history is ~60% bot commits).
8. **If a risky behavior change is unavoidable** (e.g., negative-number or dual-option heuristics), pair it with a "parser spec" test file documenting the state machine, and add migration tips — the ecosystem (commander is one of npm's most-installed packages) will surface any regression immediately.

**Success criteria for any future change**: full `npm run test-all` green (Jest + ESM smoke + type/lint/format), CI on 3 OSes, CHANGELOG entry with migration tips if user-visible, README/docs update, and typings + `tsd` updated in the same change.
"}
